Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned counsel for the respondent as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the entire record.

This criminal appeal under Section 14-A (2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellant with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection order dated 25.11.2022 passed by the Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Mahoba.

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that in this case there is allegation of maar-peet by the appellant with the victim and then to establish physical relations with her resulting into pregnancy.
Later on he refused to marry, as a result present F.I.R. was lodged.
It is further submitted that she was major and willing.

sentences.text: any force or violence was used by the appellant with her but on account of mutual dispute between the parties present F.I.R. was lodged.
Now, they have settled the dispute and living together which also appears from short counter affidavit filed by the victim herself.
The appellant is languishing in jail since 15.11.2022 having no any criminal antecedent.
Learned counsel for the appellant also referred to the amended provisions of SC/ST Act.
All these facts were not taken into consideration by the learned Special Judge while rejecting the bail which cannot be said to be lawful, therefore requested to set it aside and allow the appeal.

Learned counsel for the respondent as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid but could not dispute the fact that short counter affidavit filed by the victim herself with the fact that matter has been settled between both of them.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case submissions made by learned counsel for both the parties as well as learned A.G.A., perusal of record, it appears that the learned Special Judge has not taken into consideration all these facts while considering bail, therefore, the order passed by learned court below cannot be said to be lawful and is liable to be set-aside and the appeal is to be allowed.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is set-aside.
Let the appellant Nausad involved in Case Crime No. 521 of 2022 under Sections 323, 376, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(1)(r), 3(1)(s), 3(2) (5a) and 3(2)(5) SC/ST Act, Police Station Kotwali Nagar,
District Mahoba be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.

Further,
before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
1. The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
2. The appellant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
3. The appellant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
4. The appellant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

5. The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.
